domains.name: Aqeedah (Islamic Creed)
domains.description: Core doctrinal beliefs of Islam concerning Allah, unseen realities, divine decree, and the nature of faith and disbelief.

categories.name: Tawheed (Oneness of Allah)
categories.description: The foundational principle of monotheism in Islam — the absolute, undivided unity of Allah across all dimensions of divinity.

tags.name: Tawheed
tags.description: The indivisible oneness of Allah as the singular God, foundational to Islamic creed.

tags.name: Shirk
tags.description: The association of partners with Allah; the gravest violation of Tawheed in Islamic theology.

tags.name: Lordship of Allah
tags.description: Allah's exclusive sovereignty as creator, sustainer, and master of all existence (Rububiyyah).

tags.name: Names and Attributes of Allah
tags.description: The ninety-nine or more divine names and qualitative attributes that describe Allah's essence and actions.

tags.name: Worship of Allah Alone
tags.description: The exclusive direction of all acts of worship to Allah (Uluhiyyah), rejecting devotion to any other entity.

tags.name: Divine Majesty
tags.description: The transcendent greatness, glory, and awe-inspiring grandeur of Allah.

tags.name: Divine Perfection
tags.description: Allah's absolute flawlessness and transcendence above all deficiency or likeness to creation.

tags.name: Taghut
tags.description: False deities and powers worshipped or obeyed in defiance of Allah — rejecting Taghut is stated as the prerequisite condition alongside belief in Allah.

primary: rejecting false gods before believing in Allah
whoever rejects false deities and believes in Allah
idols and false powers worshipped besides Allah
secondary: those who seek judgment from false authorities
Satan leading people to false deities

tags.name: Alliance and Enmity in Faith
tags.description: The creedal dimension of allegiance — taking believers as allies and disavowing disbelief and its people — explicitly stated in multiple Quranic verses.

primary: prohibiting taking disbelievers as close allies
secondary: do not take disbelievers as awliya
bonds of faith over bonds of blood

categories.name: Divine Attributes and Signs
categories.description: Specific active and essential attributes of Allah as revealed in scripture, and the signs that manifest His presence.

tags.name: Divine Mercy
tags.description: Allah's encompassing compassion and forgiveness toward His creation, expressed through grace and pardon.

tags.name: Divine Knowledge
tags.description: Allah's omniscience — His complete and eternal awareness of all manifest and hidden things.

tags.name: Divine Power
tags.description: Allah's unlimited omnipotence and absolute ability over all things.

tags.name: Divine Wisdom
tags.description: Allah's perfect wisdom underlying all creation, command, and decree.

tags.name: Divine Justice
tags.description: Allah's perfect attribute of justice — His absolute fairness in judgment, decree, and recompense without any possibility of ظلم (injustice).

tags.name: Divine Will
tags.description: Allah's sovereign and unrestricted will over all that exists and all that occurs.

tags.name: Divine Signs
tags.description: Observable phenomena in creation and scripture that serve as evidence of Allah's existence and attributes.

tags.name: Divine Hearing and Seeing
tags.description: Allah's absolute and complete perception of all sounds and sights without limitation.

categories.name: Belief in the Unseen (Al-Ghayb)
categories.description: Articles of faith pertaining to realities beyond sensory perception, including angels, jinn, divine books, and metaphysical entities.

tags.name: Angels
tags.description: Belief in the angelic beings created from light who execute Allah's commands and serve specific cosmic roles.

secondary: servants of Allah in the unseen

tags.name: Jinn
tags.description: Belief in the race of sentient beings created from smokeless fire, coexisting with but invisible to humans.

tags.name: Divine Books
tags.description: Belief in the scriptures revealed by Allah to His prophets as guidance for humanity.

tags.name: Belief in the Unseen
tags.description: The overarching creedal commitment to accepting realities not accessible through direct observation or empirical means.

tags.name: Preserved Tablet
tags.description: The divine record (Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which all of creation's events are eternally inscribed.

tags.name: Throne of Allah
tags.description: The Arsh and Kursi — the supreme metaphysical stations representing Allah's dominion over creation.

tags.name: Angels Recording Deeds
tags.description: The honourable scribing angels (Kiraman Katibin) assigned to record every human action.

categories.name: Qadr (Divine Decree)
categories.description: Islamic doctrine of divine predestination — the belief that Allah has foreknown and decreed all events while humans retain moral agency.

tags.name: Divine Decree
tags.description: Allah's pre-eternal knowledge and ordainment of all events before creation.

tags.name: Human Free Will
tags.description: The capacity of humans to make real moral choices within the framework of divine decree.

tags.name: Trust in Allah
tags.description: Complete reliance upon and delegation of affairs to Allah (Tawakkul) after taking available means.

tags.name: Divine Testing
tags.description: Allah's purposeful subjection of believers to hardship or ease as a trial of faith and character.

tags.name: Contentment with Decree
tags.description: The spiritual state of being inwardly satisfied with whatever Allah has decreed.

categories.name: Faith and Disbelief
categories.description: The nature, levels, and conditions of belief and its opposite — disbelief, hypocrisy, and apostasy.

tags.name: Faith
tags.description: Iman — the sincere inner conviction in the six articles of faith, expressed in word and deed.

tags.name: Disbelief
tags.description: Kufr — the rejection or denial of the fundamental truths of Islam.

tags.name: Hypocrisy
tags.description: Nifaq — outward profession of Islam concealing inner disbelief or treachery.

tags.name: Apostasy
tags.description: Riddah — the act of consciously abandoning or renouncing Islam after having accepted it.

tags.name: Certainty of Faith
tags.description: Yaqeen — the highest degree of unwavering conviction, free from doubt.

tags.name: Increase and Decrease of Faith
tags.description: The Sunni doctrine that Iman fluctuates in strength through obedience, reflection, and sin.

categories.name: Covenant and Testimony
categories.description: The primordial covenant between Allah and humanity, and the formal declaration of faith.

tags.name: Covenant with Allah
tags.description: The primordial pledge (Mithaq) taken from all human souls before creation, affirming Allah's lordship.

tags.name: Shahada
tags.description: The Islamic declaration of faith — the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.

tags.name: Fitrah
tags.description: The innate primordial disposition of the human soul toward recognizing and inclining to Allah.

domains.name: Ibadah (Worship)
domains.description: Ritual and devotional acts prescribed in Islam — the formal practices through which believers express submission and closeness to Allah.

categories.name: Salah
categories.description: The five daily ritual prayers and supplementary devotional prayers constituting the primary act of Muslim worship.

tags.name: Obligatory Prayer
tags.description: The five daily fard prayers (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha) obligatory upon every Muslim.

tags.name: Voluntary Prayer
tags.description: Supererogatory prayers (Nafl/Sunnah) performed beyond the obligatory, including the night prayer.

tags.name: Friday Prayer
tags.description: The obligatory congregational Jumu'ah prayer performed on Fridays, replacing Dhuhr.

tags.name: Prostration
tags.description: The act of Sujud — placing the forehead on the ground as the pinnacle of submission to Allah.

tags.name: Khushu in Prayer
tags.description: The state of deep humility, focus, and spiritual presence required in prayer.

tags.name: Direction of Prayer
tags.description: The Qiblah — the obligation to face the direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah during prayer.

tags.name: Prayer Times
tags.description: The five prescribed daily time intervals within which each obligatory prayer must be performed.

tags.name: Congregational Prayer
tags.description: Praying in a group (Jama'ah) behind an Imam, which carries increased spiritual reward.

tags.name: Adhaan — Call to Prayer
tags.description: The call to prayer referenced in the Quran — including the verse on those who mock the call and the command to hasten to prayer on Friday.

primary: hasten to the remembrance of Allah on Friday
those who mock the call to prayer
secondary: come to prayer come to success
leave trade and hasten to prayer

tags.name: Eid and Celebration
tags.description: The Quranic reference to a day of celebration — the disciples of Isa requesting a table spread as an Eid — and completing worship as a cause for communal glorification of Allah.

primary: disciples asking for a feast day
completing the fast and glorifying Allah
completing the count of days and thanking Allah

categories.name: Sawm (Fasting)
categories.description: Ritual abstention from food, drink, and desires from dawn to sunset, particularly in Ramadan.

tags.name: Fasting in Ramadan
tags.description: The obligatory fast throughout the month of Ramadan, one of the five pillars of Islam.

tags.name: Voluntary Fasting
tags.description: Optional fasts performed on recommended days such as Mondays, Thursdays, or the fast of Dawud.

tags.name: Laylat al-Qadr
tags.description: The Night of Decree in the last ten nights of Ramadan, surpassing a thousand months in virtue.

tags.name: I'tikaf
tags.description: Spiritual seclusion in the mosque, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan.

tags.name: Self-Restraint through Fasting
tags.description: Fasting as a means of cultivating Taqwa through disciplined suppression of desires.

tags.name: Breaking the Fast
tags.description: The act of Iftar — ending the fast at sunset, and Suhur, the pre-dawn meal.

categories.name: Zakat and Sadaqah
categories.description: Obligatory and voluntary forms of financial worship that purify wealth and support the community.

tags.name: Obligatory Charity
tags.description: Zakat — the annual compulsory alms on qualifying wealth, one of the five pillars of Islam.

tags.name: Voluntary Charity
tags.description: Sadaqah — any voluntary act of giving for Allah's sake, including non-monetary forms.

tags.name: Zakat al-Fitr
tags.description: The obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan before Eid prayer to purify the faster.

tags.name: Spending in the Way of Allah
tags.description: Infaq fi sabilillah — expending wealth in causes pleasing to Allah, including jihad, dawah, and welfare.

tags.name: Recipients of Charity
tags.description: The eight categories of eligible recipients of Zakat as defined in Quranic scripture.

categories.name: Hajj and Umrah
categories.description: The pilgrimage rites to Makkah — the fifth pillar of Islam and its voluntary lesser form.

tags.name: Pilgrimage to Makkah
tags.description: Hajj — the obligatory annual pilgrimage to Makkah and its sacred sites, fifth pillar of Islam.

tags.name: Umrah
tags.description: The lesser pilgrimage to Makkah performable at any time of year, not obligatory but highly recommended.

tags.name: Sacrifice
tags.description: Qurbani/Udhiyah — the ritual slaughter of livestock on Eid al-Adha commemorating Ibrahim's sacrifice.

tags.name: Tawaf
tags.description: The ritual circumambulation of the Ka'bah seven times, performed in Hajj and Umrah.

tags.name: Sa'i
tags.description: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwa seven times, commemorating Hajar's search for water.

categories.name: Dhikr and Supplication
categories.description: Verbal acts of worship including remembrance of Allah, invocation, seeking forgiveness, and praise.

tags.name: Remembrance of Allah
tags.description: Dhikr — the continuous verbal and mental glorification of Allah through prescribed and spontaneous phrases.

tags.name: Supplication
tags.description: Du'a — direct personal invocation and petition to Allah, described as the essence of worship.

tags.name: Seeking Forgiveness
tags.description: Istighfar — actively seeking Allah's forgiveness through repentance and verbal appeal.

tags.name: Gratitude to Allah
tags.description: Shukr — recognizing Allah as the source of blessings and expressing thankfulness through words, worship, and obedience.

tags.name: Praising Allah
tags.description: Hamd and Tasbih — specific acts of glorifying and extolling Allah's perfection.

tags.name: Sending Blessings on the Prophet
tags.description: Salawat — invoking Allah's blessings and peace upon the Prophet Muhammad.

categories.name: Purification
categories.description: Ritual and spiritual cleanliness as prerequisites for worship and as a general Islamic value.

tags.name: Ritual Purification
tags.description: Taharah — the ritual cleanliness achieved through Wudu, Ghusl, or Tayammum required for acts of worship.

tags.name: Cleanliness
tags.description: Nazafah — general bodily and environmental hygiene promoted as part of Islamic practice.

categories.name: Oaths and Vows
categories.description: Solemn verbal commitments made by or to Allah and the legal consequences attached to them.

tags.name: Oaths
tags.description: Yameen — solemn swearing by Allah's name, with binding legal and moral implications.

secondary: not to swear by other than Allah

tags.name: Vows
tags.description: Nadhr — a voluntary pledge to Allah to perform an act conditional on a desire or as pure devotion.

tags.name: Expiation
tags.description: Kaffarah — prescribed acts of atonement for breaking oaths or other specific violations.

domains.name: Akhlaq (Ethics and Character)
domains.description: The moral and ethical framework of Islam governing virtues to cultivate, vices to avoid, and conduct toward others.

categories.name: Virtues
categories.description: Positive moral qualities praised in Islamic scripture and prophetic tradition.

tags.name: Patience
tags.description: Sabr — steadfast endurance in the face of hardship, sin-avoidance, or the demands of obedience. A comprehensive moral virtue, not limited to any single context.

tags.name: Truthfulness
tags.description: Sidq — consistency between inner conviction and outward expression; honesty in all speech and conduct.

tags.name: Humility
tags.description: Tawadu — lowering oneself before Allah and avoiding arrogance toward other humans.

tags.name: Generosity
tags.description: Karam — freely giving wealth, time, and goodness beyond what is obligated.

tags.name: Courage
tags.description: Shuja'ah — the virtue of bravery in standing for truth and facing fear in Allah's cause.

tags.name: Gentleness
tags.description: Rifq — soft, kind, and considerate treatment of others as a prophetic character trait.

tags.name: Trustworthiness
tags.description: Amanah — reliability and faithfulness in honoring all trusts, covenants, and responsibilities.

tags.name: Righteousness
tags.description: Birr — comprehensive moral goodness encompassing piety, right action, and excellent conduct.

tags.name: Hayaa (Modesty and Shame)
tags.description: The virtue of modesty and protective shame — present in Quranic verses on lowering the gaze and in the depiction of the modest woman who approached Musa in Madyan.

primary: she came to him walking with shyness
modest woman in the story of Moses
secondary: lowering gaze as expression of modesty

tags.name: Chastity (Iffah)
tags.description: Restraining oneself from forbidden desires — praised in Joseph's resistance to seduction and in direct commands to guard one's chastity.

primary: I seek refuge in Allah from this
secondary: those who cannot marry should remain chaste

categories.name: Vices
categories.description: Moral failings condemned in Islamic scripture as destructive to individuals, relationships, and communities.

tags.name: Arrogance
tags.description: Kibr — an inflated sense of self-importance that blinds one to truth and breeds contempt for others.

tags.name: Envy
tags.description: Hasad — wishing the removal of another's blessing out of resentment or spite.

tags.name: Greed
tags.description: Tama and Shuh — excessive desire for wealth and possessions, paired with miserliness.

tags.name: Lying
tags.description: Kadhib — deliberate false speech, condemned as a root of all vices in Islamic ethics.

tags.name: Backbiting
tags.description: Gheebah — mentioning a person's real faults in their absence without need or justification.

tags.name: Injustice
tags.description: Dhulm — wrongdoing that transgresses the rights of Allah, the self, or other creation.

tags.name: Extravagance
tags.description: Israf and Tabdheer — wasteful excess in consumption or spending beyond need.

tags.name: Haste
tags.description: Ajalah — acting impulsively without deliberation, contrasted with the Islamic value of measured action.

categories.name: Interpersonal Ethics
categories.description: Standards governing conduct between individuals — forgiveness, speech, respect, and trust.

tags.name: Forgiveness
tags.description: Afw — the act of pardoning others' offenses without requiring recompense.

tags.name: Good Companionship
tags.description: Selecting righteous and virtuous companions whose influence strengthens one's faith and character.

tags.name: Fulfilling Promises
tags.description: Wafa — the obligation to honor agreements and commitments made to others.

tags.name: Good Speech
tags.description: Qawl Hasanah — the Islamic standard of speaking words that are true, kind, and beneficial.

tags.name: Respecting Others
tags.description: Ikram — honoring human dignity and showing due respect to others regardless of status.

tags.name: Avoiding Suspicion
tags.description: Husn al-Dhann — cultivating good assumptions about others and avoiding baseless suspicion.

categories.name: Intention and Sincerity
categories.description: The inner dimension of action — the role of intent in determining the moral and spiritual value of deeds.

tags.name: Sincerity
tags.description: Ikhlas — performing deeds exclusively for Allah's sake, free from any desire for human recognition.

tags.name: Showing Off
tags.description: Riya — performing acts of worship to be seen or praised by people, nullifying their spiritual value.

tags.name: Correct Intention
tags.description: Niyyah — the deliberate, conscious purpose underlying an act that determines its religious validity.

tags.name: Self-Accountability
tags.description: Muhasabah — the practice of regularly examining one's own deeds, motives, and spiritual state.

categories.name: Love and Compassion
categories.description: The affective and relational dimensions of Islamic ethics — love for Allah, compassion for creation, and bonds of brotherhood.

tags.name: Love of Allah
tags.description: Hubb Allah — supreme devotional love for Allah that motivates obedience and transforms character.

tags.name: Compassion for Creation
tags.description: Rahmah — extending mercy, empathy, and care toward all of Allah's creatures.

tags.name: Brotherhood and Sisterhood
tags.description: Ukhuwwah — the bond of faith that unites believers as a single spiritual family.

tags.name: Kindness to Parents
tags.description: Birr al-Walidayn — dutiful, respectful, and loving treatment of one's parents as a supreme obligation.

domains.name: Mu'amalat (Social Relations)
domains.description: Islamic principles governing family, economic transactions, social justice, and community life.

categories.name: Family and Marriage
categories.description: Islamic framework for the family unit — marriage, parenting, kinship, and the rights of spouses and children.

tags.name: Marriage
tags.description: Nikah — the sacred contract of matrimony in Islam, establishing rights and obligations between spouses.

tags.name: Divorce
tags.description: Talaq and Khul — the lawful dissolution of marriage, governed by prescribed procedures and conditions.

tags.name: Rights of Spouses
tags.description: The mutual and reciprocal rights and obligations incumbent on husband and wife in Islamic law.

tags.name: Parenting
tags.description: Tarbiyah — the Islamic responsibility of raising children with proper moral, religious, and educational upbringing.

tags.name: Kinship Ties
tags.description: Silat al-Rahm — maintaining and nurturing bonds with extended family as a religious obligation.

tags.name: Orphan Care
tags.description: The Islamic duty to protect, care for, and justly manage the affairs of orphaned children.

categories.name: Economic Transactions
categories.description: Islamic principles governing trade, wealth, contracts, and the prohibition of exploitative financial practices.

tags.name: Fair Trade
tags.description: The Islamic ethic of honest, just, and transparent commercial dealings between parties.

tags.name: Prohibition of Riba
tags.description: The absolute Islamic prohibition of usury and interest-based transactions as exploitative and unjust.

tags.name: Wealth Management
tags.description: Islamic principles of responsible stewardship over financial resources and assets.

tags.name: Waqf
tags.description: Islamic endowment — dedicating an asset in perpetuity for charitable or religious purposes.

tags.name: Debt and Contracts
tags.description: Islamic rules governing the documentation, fulfilment, and ethics of loans and contractual agreements.

tags.name: Fraud and Cheating
tags.description: The Islamic prohibition of deceptive or manipulative practices in commercial and social dealings.

categories.name: Social Justice
categories.description: Islamic principles ensuring the equitable treatment of all people and the protection of the vulnerable.

tags.name: Justice
tags.description: Adl — the comprehensive Islamic obligation to deal equitably and without bias in all affairs.

tags.name: Rights of the Poor
tags.description: The Islamic obligation to protect the welfare of the destitute and ensure their basic needs are met.

tags.name: Rights of Neighbors
tags.description: Haqq al-Jar — specific duties and courtesies owed to those who live in proximity.

tags.name: Equality
tags.description: Musawah — the Islamic principle that all humans are equal regardless of race, tribe, or lineage.

tags.name: Combating Oppression
tags.description: The Islamic duty to oppose, resist, and seek redress against all forms of tyranny and injustice.

tags.name: Consultation
tags.description: Shura — the Islamic principle of collective deliberation and seeking counsel in decision-making.

categories.name: Community and Society
categories.description: Islamic obligations relating to moral order within society — enjoining good, forbidding evil, and fostering unity.

tags.name: Enjoining Good
tags.description: Amr bil Ma'ruf — the positive obligation to actively promote and encourage virtuous acts in society.

tags.name: Forbidding Evil
tags.description: Nahi anil Munkar — the obligation to oppose and prevent wrongdoing in society by appropriate means.

tags.name: Cooperation
tags.description: Ta'awun — mutual assistance and collaborative effort in righteousness among believers.

tags.name: Unity of the Ummah
tags.description: The imperative for Muslims to maintain communal solidarity and avoid division.

tags.name: Peace and Reconciliation
tags.description: Sulh and Islah — the Islamic imperative to resolve conflicts and restore harmony between parties.

categories.name: Inheritance and Wealth Distribution
categories.description: Islamic law governing the distribution of a deceased person's estate among rightful heirs.

tags.name: Inheritance Law
tags.description: Faraid — the divinely prescribed system of shares for distributing a deceased's estate.

tags.name: Bequests
tags.description: Wasiyyah — a testamentary gift of up to one-third of one's estate, directed to non-heirs before death.

tags.name: Wealth Circulation
tags.description: The Islamic principle that wealth must circulate and not concentrate in the hands of the few.

domains.name: Ahkam (Islamic Law)
domains.description: The sources, methodology, and substantive rulings of Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) covering permissibility, prohibition, governance, and criminal law.

categories.name: Sources of Law
categories.description: The four primary juristic sources from which Islamic legal rulings are derived.

tags.name: The Quran as Source
tags.description: The primacy of the Quran as the first and foundational source of Islamic legislation.

tags.name: The Sunnah as Source
tags.description: The prophetic traditions (Sunnah/Hadith) as the second source of Islamic law.

tags.name: Scholarly Consensus
tags.description: Ijma — the agreement of qualified Islamic scholars on a ruling, constituting a binding source of law.

tags.name: Analogical Reasoning
tags.description: Qiyas — extending a known ruling to a new case through analogy based on a shared effective cause.

categories.name: Halal and Haram
categories.description: The Islamic categories of the permissible and the prohibited across all aspects of life.

tags.name: Permissible
tags.description: Halal and Mubah — acts and things explicitly permitted or left unrestricted in Islamic law.

tags.name: Prohibited
tags.description: Haram — acts and things explicitly forbidden in Islamic law, carrying sin and legal consequences.

tags.name: Dietary Laws
tags.description: Islamic regulations specifying permissible and forbidden foods and methods of slaughter.

tags.name: Intoxicants
tags.description: The absolute Islamic prohibition on alcohol, drugs, and all mind-altering substances.

tags.name: Gambling
tags.description: The Islamic prohibition on games of chance, betting, and all forms of speculative wagering.

categories.name: Criminal Law
categories.description: Islamic penal regulations including prescribed punishments, retaliation, and rules of evidence.

tags.name: Hudud
tags.description: Fixed divinely prescribed punishments for specific major offenses mentioned in the Quran.

tags.name: Retribution
tags.description: Qisas — the principle of equal retaliation in cases of murder or physical injury.

tags.name: Blood Money
tags.description: Diyah — financial compensation paid to the victim's family as an alternative to or alongside Qisas.

tags.name: Witnesses and Evidence
tags.description: Islamic rules governing testimony, burden of proof, and the admissibility of evidence in legal proceedings.

categories.name: Jihad and Defense
categories.description: The Islamic doctrine and ethics of striving in Allah's cause, self-defense, and laws of warfare.

tags.name: Jihad
tags.description: Striving in Allah's cause — encompassing both inner spiritual struggle and outward collective effort.

tags.name: Self-Defense
tags.description: The lawful right to defend oneself, family, and community against aggression.

tags.name: Rules of War
tags.description: The ethical and legal constraints governing conduct during armed conflict in Islam.

tags.name: Peace Treaties
tags.description: The legitimacy and conditions of entering into truces and peace agreements with adversaries.

tags.name: Migration for Faith
tags.description: Hijrah — the migration from a place of religious oppression to preserve one's faith and practice.

tags.name: Martyrdom
tags.description: The status of those killed in Allah's cause — their souls alive with their Lord, not to be called dead — a distinct theological category addressed directly in the Quran.

primary: killed in the way of Allah
do not say they are dead
those who die in Allah's cause
secondary: rejoicing in what Allah has given them
reward for those slain in His cause

categories.name: Governance
categories.description: Islamic principles of political authority, leadership obligations, and the ruler-citizen relationship.

tags.name: Leadership
tags.description: The Islamic conception of legitimate political and religious leadership through Khilafah or Imamah.

tags.name: Obedience to Authority
tags.description: The conditional Islamic obligation to obey legitimate rulers and those in authority.

tags.name: Accountability of Rulers
tags.description: The Islamic principle that leaders are accountable to Allah and to the community for just governance.

domains.name: Tazkiyah (Spiritual Purification)
domains.description: The inward dimension of Islamic practice — purifying the soul, healing the heart, and drawing closer to Allah through spiritual discipline.

categories.name: Heart and Soul
categories.description: The spiritual states and conditions of the human heart as the center of faith and moral life.

tags.name: Purification of the Heart
tags.description: Tazkiyat al-Nafs — the ongoing process of cleansing the soul from spiritual diseases and moral failings.

tags.name: Diseases of the Heart
tags.description: Amrad al-Qulub — spiritual pathologies such as envy, riya, and hardness of heart that corrupt the soul.

tags.name: Softness of Heart
tags.description: Leen al-Qalb — the tender, receptive heart moved by remembrance of Allah and Quranic recitation.

tags.name: Consciousness of Allah
tags.description: Taqwa — the ever-present awareness of Allah that motivates righteous action and restraint from sin.

tags.name: Contentment
tags.description: Qana'ah — inner satisfaction with what Allah has provided, free from restless craving.

categories.name: Repentance and Return
categories.description: The processes of turning back to Allah after sin — repentance, hope, fear, and spiritual balance.

tags.name: Repentance
tags.description: Tawbah — sincere turning away from sin toward Allah, meeting the conditions of genuine repentance.

tags.name: Return to Allah
tags.description: Inabah — a deeper, proactive turning of the entire self toward Allah in devotion.

tags.name: Hope in Allah's Mercy
tags.description: Raja — the spiritual state of confident hope in Allah's forgiveness and generosity.

tags.name: Fear of Allah
tags.description: Khawf and Khashyah — reverent awe and fear of Allah's punishment and displeasure.

tags.name: Balance of Hope and Fear
tags.description: The spiritually healthy state between Raja (hope) and Khawf (fear), avoiding both despair and false security.

categories.name: Spiritual Struggle
categories.description: The internal and external battles of the believer against the nafs, worldly temptation, and satanic whispering.

tags.name: Struggling Against the Nafs
tags.description: Mujahadah — the deliberate effort to resist the soul's inclinations toward sin and heedlessness.

tags.name: Temptation
tags.description: The lures of worldly allure and shaytan's whispers that lead believers away from obedience.

tags.name: Worldly Attachment
tags.description: Hubb al-Dunya — excessive love of the material world that distracts from the Hereafter.

tags.name: Zuhd
tags.description: Ascetic detachment from the world — not owning less, but the world owning less of the heart.

categories.name: Closeness to Allah
categories.description: The spiritual stations and practices through which a believer draws nearer to Allah.

tags.name: Yearning for Allah
tags.description: Shawq — an intense spiritual longing for closeness to Allah and for meeting Him in the Hereafter.

tags.name: Obedience to Allah
tags.description: Ta'ah — comprehensive submission to Allah's commands and prohibitions as the path to His nearness.

tags.name: Night Worship
tags.description: Qiyam al-Layl/Tahajjud — voluntary night prayers as a means of special closeness to Allah.

tags.name: Contemplation
tags.description: Tafakkur — the inner devotional act of sustained deep reflection as a form of worship that draws the believer into greater spiritual closeness with Allah.

tags.name: Spiritual Elevation
tags.description: The attainment of high spiritual stations (Maqamat) and nearness to Allah through sustained devotion.

domains.name: Akhirah (The Hereafter)
domains.description: Islamic eschatology — the sequence of events from death through resurrection, judgment, and the eternal destinations of Paradise and Hell.

categories.name: Death and the Grave
categories.description: The transition from worldly life to the intermediate realm (Barzakh) following death.

tags.name: Death
tags.description: Mawt — the inevitable end of worldly life and separation of soul from body, the beginning of Akhirah.

tags.name: Life of the Grave
tags.description: Barzakh — the intermediate realm between death and resurrection, where souls experience bliss or punishment.

tags.name: Angel of Death
tags.description: Malak al-Mawt — the angel tasked with extracting souls at their appointed time of death.

tags.name: Shroud and Burial
tags.description: The Islamic rites surrounding the preparation and burial of the deceased.

categories.name: Day of Judgment
categories.description: The events of Yawm al-Qiyamah — resurrection, reckoning, weighing of deeds, and crossing the Sirat.
